visual_anchor_inventory.description: Upper-left corner ornate fan/mace-shaped object. Resembles a decorative parasol or funnel-top collector. Rendered in pale yellow-brown with blue bead details. Connected to horizontal pipe chain running right. This is the LEFT INLET — source side of the pipe network.

Upper-right corner mirror-image fan/mace apparatus. Also a fan/parasol collector. Pale yellow-brown, blue bead trim. Connected to a red cylindrical vessel below it via a tube. This is the RIGHT INLET — secondary source or parallel inlet branch.

Horizontal pipe/tube chain running across the top of the folio connecting upper-left fan apparatus to the upper-right zone. Consists of segmented cylindrical barrel-shaped sections (rendered in pale grey/white with brown outline) connected by red/crimson ring joints. This is the MAIN HORIZONTAL DISTRIBUTION CONDUIT. Flow direction: LEFT to RIGHT (left fan = input, right zone = output to upper-right vessel). Two visible red ring connectors act as valve/junction points.

valve_joints.note: T-junction or simple coupling — no branch visible, likely a sealing ring
Second coupling before the right descent tube

visual_anchor_inventory.description: Vertical tube descending from the horizontal pipe chain on the right side, feeding liquid DOWN into the upper pool/tub. Rendered in blue-green ink indicating fluid presence. Connects upper_right_fan_apparatus area down to upper_pool_tub. This is the PRIMARY INFLOW TUBE to the upper pool.
visual_anchor_inventory.note: The blue-green coloring of this tube is a SEMANTIC MARKER: blue/green = liquid in active flow state. Compare with qo- prefix concentration in the text paragraph to the left of this tube.

visual_anchor_inventory.description: Cylindrical red/crimson vessel or cup positioned below the upper-right fan apparatus. Wide-rimmed, open-top cup shape. visual_anchor_inventory.note: Red vessel = possible thermal/reactive state marker. Cross-reference with any 'char-' or 'dar-' prefix words in adjacent text.

visual_anchor_inventory.description: Large oval/circular pool in the middle-right of the folio (~40% down the page). Filled with GREEN wash. Contains approximately 8-10 nude female nymph figures (white/cream skin, rendered in outline ink) bathing, floating, and interacting within the green liquid. The pool has a defined circular border with brown ink outline. The right_descent_tube feeds into the TOP of this pool. The neck_connector_tube exits from the BOTTOM. Semantically: GREEN LIQUID = herbal bath or preparation pool.

Narrow vertical NECK tube connecting the upper_pool_tub (exit at bottom) to the lower_pool_tub (entry at top). This is the critical FLOW CONDUIT between the two pools. Rendered in blue-green ink. The neck appears constricted — suggesting a controlled flow rate or valve effect. Visible at approximately x=600-640, y=670-790. This is the structural anchor for the bisection in f78r.36.
visual_anchor_inventory.note: BISECTION ANCHOR for f78r.36 <->: the text 'qol<->saiin' is split by this neck tube. LEFT side: 'qol' (qo- outflow prefix), RIGHT side: 'saiin' (sa-/so- inflow/collection prefix). This is a CRITICAL SEMANTIC GROUNDING: the bisection physically encodes the transition from OUTFLOW (upper pool draining) to INFLOW (lower pool filling).

visual_anchor_inventory.description: Second oval/circular pool in the lower-right quadrant of the folio (~80% down the page). Also filled with GREEN wash. Contains approximately 6-8 nude female nymph figures. Slightly smaller than the upper pool. Receives inflow from neck_connector_tube. No visible outflow tube — this appears to be the TERMINAL COLLECTION VESSEL. The pool border is brown ink outline.

Thin vertical tube or channel running along the right margin, roughly parallel to the right_descent_tube but further right. Blue-green ink. Partially cut off by page edge. May represent a secondary drain or overflow channel from the upper_pool_tub.
visual_anchor_inventory.note: Uncertain function. If this is an overflow outlet, it would correspond to a 'safety valve' in the apparatus. Watch for 'or' / 'ol' suffixed words in f78r.16 and f78r.47 which may label this.

visual_anchors.morphology_description: Ornate fan or mace-shaped collector at top-left. Resembles an inverted parasol or sprinkler head. The fan ribs spread upward and outward. Blue bead decorations on the ribs. The base connects directly to the leftmost segment of the horizontal pipe chain. FUNCTION: inlet collector — possibly representing a water source, rain collector, or distillation condenser top.

Mirror-image fan apparatus at top-right. Same morphology as upper-left fan. Base connects to a red cylindrical cup/vessel below it, which in turn feeds the right_descent_tube. FUNCTION: secondary inlet or parallel source branch. The right-side red cup intermediary suggests a different material state (heated or reactive) for the right branch vs. the left.

Segmented horizontal pipe running top of folio. Individual segments are barrel/cylinder shaped (~40-50 units long each), rendered in pale grey with brown outlines. Red ring joints at two points serve as couplings or T-junctions. No visible branching — these are inline couplings, not T-valves. FLOW: left-to-right. The pipe appears to carry the collected liquid from the left fan toward the right descent tube.

Vertical tube, right side, descending from horizontal pipe chain to the upper pool. BLUE-GREEN coloring is the semantic key: this color is consistently used in f78r for ACTIVE LIQUID FLOW. The tube has a smooth, uninterrupted profile — no valve or constriction. Terminates at the top rim of upper_pool_tub.

Small cylindrical red cup between the right fan and descent tube. Open top, wide rim. No lid. Red color signals either: (a) heated vessel / warming bath, (b) a specific reactive preparation (e.g., acid, wine-based). Its position as an INTERMEDIARY between inlet and vertical tube suggests it functions as a pre-treatment or temperature-conditioning stage.

Large oval bathing pool, middle-right. GREEN wash fills the interior. ~9 female nymph figures visible: standing, reclining, reaching. The pool rim is a clean circular border. The inflow enters from the top-right (right_descent_tube). The outflow neck exits from the bottom-center. GREEN = herbal or mineral-infused liquid (consistent with balneological/pharmaceutical preparation). The nymphs likely encode procedural actors or measurement states.

Critical narrow neck tube connecting the two pools vertically. Constricted profile at the mid-point — this morphological narrowing is consistent with a flow-control valve or siphon. The bisection of f78r.36 occurs HERE: 'qol' (left side of tube = outflow/drain from upper pool) and 'saiin' (right side = inflow/fill to lower pool). This is the ONLY point in the entire apparatus where a flow-state TRANSITION is textually encoded at the pixel level.

Smaller oval collection pool at the bottom of the folio. GREEN wash interior, ~7 nymphs. No visible outflow tube — this is the TERMINAL COLLECTION VESSEL of the entire apparatus. The nymphs here may encode a final product state or measurement. The absence of an outflow tube is semantically significant: the process terminates here (product collected / preparation complete).

Thin vertical blue-green channel along right margin. Uncertain function: either a parallel drain from the upper pool or an overflow safety channel. Partially cut off by page edge. No text labels directly attached in the transcription, but proximity to @Lt label zone right margin suggests it may be annotated by f78r.47 ('okaral').
